The browser and FM-1 keep separate User Banks. Connect with USB to use the hardware banks.

Hardware editing needs the 1.1 editor firmware and Web MIDI with SysEx (Chrome or Edge). Audio comes from the FM-1 while connected; the small display is a live parameter view. Full .mddb backups contain the saved project, preferences and all User Banks; unsaved live edits, granular audio and calibration are excluded. A full restore requires STOP, internal clock, and physical SEL confirmation. Save changes before backing up, or export the live patch separately.

Hold a function button to see its controls explained on the display. Tap to use it. EDIT: Sound → Filter → Envelope → Mix. SEQ: Rhythm → Groove. FX: Granular → Tape. GLO: Harmony → System → Look. HOME + PRESET: Biome. EDIT + PRESET: sound preset. Every track can use every engine.

Begin with Blank or any factory Biome. Shape your six voices and phrases, then use GLO → User Banks to select one of 16 Biome slots or 64 sound slots. Enter a name, stop playback, choose internal clock and save. In browser mode, an occupied slot requires a second Save within three seconds. The live FM-1 editor instead asks you to confirm replacement. Browser banks stay in this browser; hardware banks stay on the FM-1. Export each finished Biome as a file for safekeeping. Granular audio is not stored.

GROWING THROUGH YOUR FEEDBACK

Thank you for listening.

Your response to Mutable Dreams has shaped this next chapter. Your requests for warmer sounds, personal Biomes and dependable performance are at the heart of 1.1. Thank you for making music with it, and for telling us what could be better.

Every voice is yours.

Fill all six tracks with percussion, resonant strings, soft chords, or any combination. Choose from 272 sound presets while keeping your notes, rhythm, levels and sends. An empty Biome is a starting point for a world of your own.

Chance, with a memory.

Euclidean patterns, swing, accents and repeats meet eight shared scales. Lock a seed with ARP, make a variation with REC, and undo it with ENV. Freeze, reverse or transpose the granular cloud as your rhythm keeps moving.

Room to be clear.

Full-rate granular recording, gently overlapping grains and a cleaner signal path bring more detail. Open the filter for clarity or close it for warmth. Gentle resonance and fundamental-led presets keep softer sounds within easy reach. FULL offers richer processing; dense combinations automatically use ECO to protect playback on the FM-1.

WITH GRATITUDE / OUR ROOTS

From a generous idea,
new worlds can grow.

Mutable Dreams owes its foundations to Émilie Gillet and Mutable Instruments. Their instruments and openly shared code made this exploration possible. Selected original algorithms from Plaits, Rings and the new Elements Strike subset form part of our sound engine, with their original credits and MIT notices preserved.

Our contribution is a six-voice instrument for the FM-1: editable Biomes, generative rhythms, a custom granular bus, and an interface that invites discovery. We want to carry that spirit of curiosity into something approachable, expressive, and unmistakably its own.

Explore the original source ↗Discover Plaits ↗Discover Rings ↗

An independent community project, unaffiliated with and not endorsed by Mutable Instruments. These are selected algorithms, not complete module ports. Our granular bus and Round Bass are our own designs. Marbles-inspired remembered variation, Tides-inspired cyclic modulation and Warps-inspired ring blending are original implementations, not complete ports of those modules.

Mutable Dreams · Independent firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1. Selected DSP: Émilie Gillet / Mutable Instruments, MIT. Device platform and simulator: fm1-base / felucca-bsp, MPL-2.0. This browser runs the firmware sound engine; FM-1 performance is measured separately. Browser saves stay on this computer. 16 named User Biomes and 64 user sound slots; factory Biomes remain available. Export your finished Biomes as files for safekeeping. Granular memory: 2.97 seconds, mono PCM16 at 44.1 kHz, with stereo grains. ECO uses half-rate FM / VA / Harmonic voices. Read the measurements and limitations ↗
